protocols.title: Debt/credit burdens and subsequent systemic banking crises
protocols.definition: Higher private-credit burden and weaker external positions are associated with higher later systemic-banking-crisis onset risk.
protocols.scientific_rationale: Long debt-cycle mechanisms predict repayment stress before financial-system breakdown.
protocols.target_outcome: source-defined systemic banking crisis onset (initially JST crisisJST=1)

research_population.selection_rule: predefined JST R6 source coverage; outcomes were not used to select countries

predictor_variables.transformation: lagged level and five-year change; source units preserved

information_cutoff_rules.leakage_guard: predictor period < outcome year; dataset-version fixed to JST R6

forecast_horizons.event: onset only; ongoing-crisis state is separate

protocols.falsification_criteria: No out-of-sample discrimination above base rate or an exploratory-only result is evidence inconsistent with predictive value.
known_limitations: IMF 2026 dataset unavailable at implementation time

protocols.title: Institutional deterioration and later investment/productivity weakness
protocols.definition: WGI deterioration and inequality/institutional proxies are candidates for predicting later investment or productivity weakness.
protocols.scientific_rationale: Internal-order theory links institutional cohesion to productive capacity.
protocols.target_outcome: independently defined persistent productivity/investment weakness (outcome registry not yet populated)
protocols.falsification_criteria: Unavailable outcome evidence means untestable, not supported.

protocols.title: Relative international-power convergence and rivalry/crisis risk
protocols.definition: Power convergence between major states may precede independently dated rivalry, conflict or order-transition episodes.
protocols.target_outcome: independent rivalry, conflict or order-transition outcome registry (not populated)
protocols.falsification_criteria: No independent outcome evidence means untestable.

protocols.title: Recurring long sequences of monetary, domestic and external order changes
protocols.definition: Historical orders may recur through a long sequence spanning decades to centuries.
protocols.scientific_rationale: The broad Big Cycle claim motivates separated long-run measurements.
protocols.target_outcome: independently dated complete order-transition cycles (not populated)
protocols.falsification_criteria: Current evidence cannot test a universal duration or deterministic sequence.
known_limitations: no consistent multi-century entities or outcomes
